clue.text: Prepares to shoot at 26 battle for crest

parts.note: a gunman cocks a weapon to make it ready to fire

indicators.note: the answer to 26 across is the word lost, so the word at goes missing from the battle word

parts.note: a battle is combat
taken as written

explanation.surface: A soldier readies his gun for a lost battle and wins a crest.
explanation.walkthrough: The cross-reference '26' stands for its answer, LOST, which serves as the removal signal: COMBAT with AT lost leaves COMB.
explanation.definitionFit: A cockscomb is the fleshy red crest on a rooster's head.

clue.text: California alley turned when changing sides, like the Vicar of Bray

definitions.text: when changing sides, like the Vicar of Bray

parts.note: CA is the postal abbreviation for California
Tin Pan Alley, the songwriting district, with the alley turned away leaves its first two words

explanation.surface: A Californian back street changes direction, recalling a famous turncoat cleric.
explanation.walkthrough: TIN PAN ALLEY was New York's popular-music district. To 'turn cat in pan' is an old phrase for switching sides; the Vicar of Bray, in an English folk song, changed his religion with every new monarch to keep his job.
explanation.definitionFit: Turning cat in pan is an archaic idiom for deserting one's party, exactly what the turncoat vicar of the song kept doing.

clue.text: See 5
Sudden increase, said about new piece of DNA by top operator

parts.note: a surge is a sudden rise

indicators.note: about tells us the spoken word goes round the next pieces

parts.note: oral means spoken rather than written
a gene is a stretch of DNA

explanation.surface: A spike in a new DNA fragment is announced by a leading geneticist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Top operator' looks like a skilled person in general, but it means the chief medical officer, the head 'surgeon'.
explanation.definitionFit: A Surgeon General is the chief medical official of a country or service, playfully the head of all surgeons.

clue.text: Had no business to remove top of branch with explosive

indicators.note: taking off the top of a word means its first letter goes

parts.note: a bough is a tree branch
TNT is the explosive trinitrotoluene

explanation.surface: Someone should never have lopped a branch with dynamite.
explanation.definitionFit: Saying someone oughtn't to do a thing means they had no right or business doing it.

clue.text: Phallic bunion has enabled one to have a smashing time

definitions.text: one to have a smashing time

indicators.note: the letters are enabled to take a new shape, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: An absurd swollen foot somehow lets someone have great fun.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Smashing time' looks like British slang for a great time, but it is literal: a clumsy beast breaking crockery. The anagram signal 'enabled' rearranges PHALLIC BUNION HAS.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes a clumsy person who wrecks delicate things, someone literally smashing crockery.

clue.text: See 5
Maximum awareness required when the H. Grail is exposed

indicators.note: exposed here suggests the letters are laid open and rearranged

explanation.surface: Everyone must be on guard when the Holy Grail is revealed.
explanation.walkthrough: The rearrangement signal is 'exposed', working on THE H GRAIL.
explanation.definitionFit: Being on high alert means being in a state of the greatest watchfulness.

clue.text: Bribery sees Italian girl encompassing end of Italy

indicators.note: encompassing means the girl's name surrounds the next piece

parts.note: Paola is an Italian girl's name

indicators.note: end of picks the final letter of the word

explanation.surface: An Italian woman is paid off, with Italy itself involved.
explanation.definitionFit: Payola is a slang term for bribes, especially those paid to get records played on radio.

clue.text: Infer one has to cry to utility regulator being unable to breathe

indicators.note: the word Infer is split so that in tells us the rest goes round the next pieces

parts.note: the letters after in, taken as written
I is the Roman numeral one
to shout is to cry out
Ofwat is the British regulator of the water industry

explanation.surface: Someone guesses that a customer must complain to the water watchdog.
explanation.walkthrough: The trick is to split 'Infer' as 'In' (the insertion signal) plus FER. OFWAT is the body overseeing water companies in England and Wales.
explanation.definitionFit: A fish out of water literally cannot breathe; figuratively the phrase means someone uncomfortable in unfamiliar surroundings.

clue.text: I'll have a go at being part-commander of old Greek ship

indicators.note: only part of the word is used, its last four letters dropped

parts.note: a trierarch commanded an ancient Greek trireme

explanation.surface: Someone volunteers to play a captain of an ancient galley.
explanation.walkthrough: A TRIERARCH commanded a trireme; taking only part of the title leaves TRIER, with ARCH dropped.
explanation.definitionFit: A trier is a person who makes an effort, the sort who says they will give something a go.

clue.text: Miserably niggly about everything so as to cause irritation

indicators.note: about tells us the jumbled letters go round the next piece
miserably suggests the letters are in a wretched, disordered state

parts.note: all means everything

explanation.surface: Someone nitpicks wretchedly about everything, annoying everyone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Miserably' makes GINGLY from the jumbled letters, and 'about' wraps it round the word for everything.
explanation.definitionFit: Galling means irritating or vexing, so gallingly means in an annoying manner.

clue.text: Neighbours are in a home

definitions.note: a plural noun; the answer is used as a noun for one's closest people

indicators.note: in places the word are within the home

parts.note: a nest is a home, for birds
taken as written

explanation.surface: People living next door are in one house.
explanation.walkthrough: As in 'nearest and dearest', the answer serves as a noun for those closest at hand.
explanation.definitionFit: Those nearest to you are the people living closest, your neighbours.

clue.text: Outlaw is king when field's reversed

parts.note: taken as written
HM stands for His Majesty, the king

indicators.note: reversed means the word for field is read backwards

parts.note: a lea is a meadow or field; the 's is a link

explanation.surface: A royal becomes an outcast when the land is turned upside down.
explanation.definitionFit: Ishmael, son of Abraham, was cast out into the desert, so the name means an outcast.

clue.text: First increase height, absorbing nitrogen, which is misplaced like the creatures in the puzzle

definitions.text: misplaced like the creatures in the puzzle

parts.note: A is first, as in a top grade
to gain is to increase

indicators.note: absorbing means the height word takes in the next letter

parts.note: stature is height
N is the chemical symbol for nitrogen

explanation.surface: Grow taller by taking in nitrogen, like the out-of-place animals here.
explanation.walkthrough: The theme answers each put an animal where it does not belong: a fish out of water, a bull in a china shop, a dog in the manger.
explanation.definitionFit: Something against nature is unnatural, like animals placed where they do not belong.

clue.text: Flew unperturbed when fool went around in a terrible state

indicators.note: went around means the fool word surrounds the scrambled letters

parts.note: an ass is a fool

indicators.note: the word unperturbed is split, leaving perturbed to rearrange the letters before it

explanation.surface: An idiot flew calmly round while things were dreadful.
explanation.walkthrough: Split 'unperturbed' as UN plus the anagram signal 'perturbed'; the jumble WFULNE goes inside the word for fool, signalled by 'went around'.
explanation.definitionFit: Awfulness is the quality of being dreadful, so a terrible state.

clue.text: Skill in right weapon gets quick answer

indicators.note: in puts the skill word within the others

parts.note: an epee is a fencing sword
art means skill

explanation.surface: A fencer with the right blade can strike back fast.
explanation.definitionFit: Repartee is quick witty reply, banter traded fast.

clue.text: Do begin with change in condition — but breast is better

indicators.note: in places the jumble within the condition word

parts.note: fettle is condition, as in fine fettle

indicators.note: with change says the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Advice to new mothers: start with a change, though breastfeeding is best.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with change' makes EDINGBO; 'in' puts it inside the condition word. The definition plays on the slogan 'breast is best'.
explanation.definitionFit: A baby's milk bottle is the alternative to breastfeeding that the slogan 'breast is best' plays down.

clue.text: Understanding isn't over the horizon

definitions.meaning: a deep perception or grasp of something
read as two words, visible and close enough to be seen

explanation.definitionFit: Insight is perceptive understanding; read as two words it means visible, so not beyond the horizon.

clue.text: Duchess of Cornwall's sister, one who died taking Camilla's part

parts.note: a goner is someone dead or doomed

indicators.note: only part of the name is taken, a couple of letters from its middle

parts.note: the name taken as written, its 's a link

explanation.surface: A royal relative dies while playing Camilla's role.
explanation.walkthrough: Camilla was the real Duchess of Cornwall, but here the duchess is Regan in King Lear, wife of the Duke of Cornwall. 'part' keeps only IL from CAMILLA, dropping CAM and LA.
explanation.definitionFit: In King Lear, Regan is Duchess of Cornwall and Goneril is her elder sister.

clue.text: Steamy talk requires a sedative

indicators.note: requires suggests the phrase contains what is needed within it

explanation.surface: Racy conversation calls for something calming.
explanation.definitionFit: Amytal is a trade name for amobarbital, a barbiturate sedative.

clue.text: Sound of river diversion in old Portuguese money

indicators.note: sound of says the word is heard rather than spelt

parts.note: a millrace is a channel diverting water to drive a mill wheel

explanation.surface: Diverting a river is heard in old Portuguese coins.
explanation.definitionFit: The milreis was the former monetary unit of Portugal and Brazil.

clue.text: Brainwave helps to make one wide awake

indicators.note: helps to make says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A flash of inspiration helps keep someone alert.
explanation.definitionFit: A brainwave is a sudden bright thought, a fresh notion.

clue.text: Love to trap other people in peril, showing selfish character

indicators.note: in places these pieces within the peril word

parts.note: danger means peril
O is love, a score of nil in tennis
a gin is a snare or trap
them means other people

explanation.surface: Love lures outsiders into danger, revealing a selfish nature.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to' and 'showing' are links; the three pieces sit after the D of the peril word, signalled by 'in'.
explanation.definitionFit: A dog in the manger begrudges others what it cannot use itself, a byword for selfishness.

clue.text: See 23
Too spirited to be miserly?

definitions.meaning: having had too many spirits, so drunk

explanation.definitionFit: Tight is slang for drunk and also means stingy with money.

clue.text: See good guy in hell?

parts.note: lo is an old word for see or behold
ST abbreviates saint, a good person

explanation.surface: Behold a virtuous man in the underworld.
explanation.walkthrough: A saint in hell would be out of place, and the damned are lost souls.
explanation.definitionFit: Souls in hell are described as lost, damned beyond saving.

clue.text: Limits of liberalism?

definitions.meaning: permitted margins of variation, as in engineering
a broad-minded acceptance of other views

explanation.definitionFit: Tolerance means both an allowable margin of error and broad-minded acceptance of others.
